That range was correct at HEAD, but receipt.py gained 8 lines at line 75 this round, so the hard-coded citation went stale. Every hash, count and list claim in the document still verifies.

Document header claim '不含手写路径' (no hand-written paths) is false as stated: §4's 11 excluded paths are hard-coded in the generator's EXCLUDED tuple, §5 step 1 hard-codes the literal '20 个路径', and §1/§2 hard-code the source line ranges. Currently '20' happens to equal len(freeze), but it will silently go stale if the freeze set changes (exactly how the line-range citation went stale). The generator should compute these or the claim should be narrowed to '§1-§3 coverage sets contain no hand-written paths'.

§2's aggregate rule is under-specified: 'canonical JSON' must mean json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')); with Python's default separators an independent reproducer gets 76e778b2025ca66b2a9a55b8e3992782f35940bac7dabdd8419831687ecf361f instead of the stated d3f283d4... Spelling out 'compact, no whitespace' would make §2 independently recomputable from prose alone.

Traceability hazard (not a freeze defect): the excluded directory CODE/work/WP-LEO-V2-PRE-EXPERIMENT-TRUST/_r4/shadow/ contains a full copy of the platform source tree. 12 of 13 sampled frozen files are byte-identical to the frozen working tree, but _r4/shadow/CODE/leo_sim/trace.py (66592 B) matches neither HEAD nor the frozen CODE/leo_sim/trace.py (67566 B). A reviewer diffing the shadow against the freeze could be misled; the shadow should be labelled as a scratch snapshot.
